object: Bellota Hunting Axe 1.5 lb with handle
how_material_identity_is_carried: material MAT_<key>, kept in the file with a fake user

parts.real_material: forged plain-carbon tool steel, quenched and tempered; head polished + lacquered (Bellota: 'Tratamiento de la cabeza: Pulido y lacado')
European beech, Fagus sylvatica, varnished ('Madera de haya', PEFC) - NOT walnut; walnut is only the nearest key in the vocabulary
beech wedge, end grain exposed at the eye mouth

textures.kind: PROCEDURAL - there are no image texture files in this project
textures.uv_maps: none; the meshes have no UV layer
textures.wood: ShaderNodeTexNoise + Mapping + ColorRamp on generated coordinates, noise stretched along Y (the handle axis) to give grain
textures.head: ShaderNodeAttribute reads the per-vertex FLOAT attribute 'u_from_edge' (distance from the cutting edge, baked by bx_pbr.bake_u_from_edge) into MapRange -> MixShader, giving the polished bit / lacquered body split on ONE forging
textures.consequence: the look travels ONLY inside the .blend; an OBJ/STL/glTF export loses it, because 'u_from_edge' is mesh data those formats cannot carry

measured_from.head.lacquer: median over the lacquered region of references/amazon_8133_SL1500.jpg, n=768977 px; the 35th, 50th and 65th percentiles are all (31,31,31) - a flat neutral matte black with no measurable spread
measured_from.head.polished: 65th percentile over the polished ground bit of the same photograph, n=136794 px (median 193,191,192); the 65th because the render adds its own shading on top of a photograph that already has some
measured_from.beech.face: median over the varnished-beech region of references/bellota_8133_SZ1.png with the burned BELLOTA mark excluded, n=179431 px
measured_from.beech.endgrain: INFERRED, not measured - the wedge's exposed end is inside the retail blister in every photograph found

two_finishes_on_one_part: Bellota's head is ONE forging with TWO finishes ('Tratamiento de la cabeza: Pulido y lacado').  An object carries one ob.color, so the Workbench `real` pass could not show both and the manifest previously flagged it.  RESOLVED IN SHADING ONLY: bx_pbr.bake_u_from_edge writes each vertex's true distance from the cutting edge into a FLOAT ATTRIBUTE and the head's shader mixes lacquer into polished across the MEASURED grind boundary at 20.14 mm.  The boundary follows the convex cutting edge rather than a plane of constant x, because the edge curves back ~12 mm at the toe and heel.  The head is NOT split - inventing a seam would put a boundary in the EM asset that the forging does not have.  An attribute is not geometry; the voxeliser reads triangles.
grain_direction: the beech shader stretches its noise along Y, the handle axis - the same grain direction the material gap records, because wood's permittivity along the grain is 15-25% higher than across it.  Keeping the render and the material note consistent.

material_gaps.real_material: forged plain-carbon tool steel, quenched and tempered ('acero forjado ... tratamiento termico', Bellota)
material_gaps.gap: THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL GAP ON THIS OBJECT.  The `steel` key carries eps_r 1.0 and sigma 1.45e6 S/m and NO mu_r at all, i.e. mu_r = 1 by omission.  Forged carbon tool steel is strongly ferromagnetic: mu_r is of order 1e2-1e3 at low field and still ~40-100 at 1-13 GHz once Snoek/ferromagnetic-resonance roll-off is accounted for.
material_gaps.why_it_matters: Surface impedance Zs = sqrt(j*omega*mu/sigma), so Zs scales as sqrt(mu_r).  Taking mu_r = 100 instead of 1 raises Re(Zs) by a factor of 10 and drops the skin depth by the same factor (delta = sqrt(2/(omega*mu*sigma)): at 1 GHz, 13.2 um at mu_r = 1 against 1.3 um at mu_r = 100).  On an object that is 80% of its mass one steel forging, that misstates the loss of the entire scatterer.
material_gaps.action: the key `steel` is used as specified; mu_r is REPORTED here and must be set in the FDTD material table, it cannot be expressed in the vocabulary.
material_gaps.appearance_note: the two finishes are resolved in the COLOUR layer only (see appearance.two_finishes_on_one_part).  Electrically they are the same steel and the same one part; the differential-hardening gap below is the electrical question and it is still open.

material_gaps.real_material: the same forging, but the bit is heat treated harder than the body
material_gaps.gap: Bellota states the head is forged in ONE piece with heat treatment; if the bit is differentially hardened its mu_r and sigma differ from the body's (martensite has lower sigma and lower mu_r than the tempered body).  One key cannot express both, and the head is one part, so it cannot be split without inventing a boundary no reference shows.

material_gaps.real_material: European beech, Fagus sylvatica - Bellota's own technical sheet says 'Madera de haya', and the Spanish general catalogue says 'Mangos de madera de Haya barnizados ... Certificado PEFC'
material_gaps.gap: Two separate problems.  (1) SPECIES: the vocabulary's only wood key is `walnut` at eps_r 2.2, sigma 0.012.  Beech is denser than walnut (0.72 vs 0.64 g/cm3) and its permittivity is correspondingly higher - published beech at 12% MC is eps_r ~2.4-2.9 across 1-13 GHz, so the key is 10-30% low.  (2) ANISOTROPY AND MOISTURE: wood is not isotropic.  Along the grain eps_r is typically 15-25% higher than across it, and eps_r rises steeply with moisture content - roughly +0.1 per 1% MC below fibre saturation, so a handle at 8% MC and the same handle at 16% MC differ by nearly a full unit of eps_r and about a factor of two in loss tangent.  On a 350 mm rod at 1-13 GHz (lambda 23-300 mm, so the handle is 1.2-15 wavelengths long) that is not negligible.
material_gaps.action: `walnut` used as the nearest key, with the species, the assumed 12% moisture content and the grain direction stated here.

material_gaps.real_material: varnish/lacquer - 'mango de madera pulida y barnizada' (Bellota); finish 'Barnizado'
material_gaps.gap: A thin dielectric film, order 30-80 um, eps_r ~3. At 13 GHz that is 0.003 of a wavelength.
material_gaps.action: OMITTED as sub-wavelength; listed in omitted_parts with the wavelength argument.

material_gaps.real_material: UNCONFIRMED.  Bellota states only 'Tipo de enmangado: Cuna' for this reference.  Bellota's Spanish premium ranges (Proline, Vizcaina 8130, Poda 8131, Garden Line) advertise a 'cuna de fibra de vidrio PATENTADA ... su fibra de vidrio y poliamida', i.e. a glass-filled polyamide wedge.  The 8133 is the Central-America 'Labor entera' line and carries no such badge in the CEN catalogue.
material_gaps.gap: If this reference is in fact fitted with the fibreglass wedge, its key changes from `walnut` (2.2 / 0.012) to something near `g10` (4.5 / 0.011) or `nylon` (2.9 / 0.002) - roughly a doubling of eps_r in a 4.29 cm3 part.
material_gaps.action: modelled as beech, matching the handle.  The part is 4286 mm3, so switching the key changes only that volume; the alternative is recorded here so it can be switched without rebuilding.
